## Work tracking
Use the live **status:**, **priority:** and **complexity:** labels above; **Assignees** identifies the owner. These labels are separate from the task/ticket type.

**Planning complexity:** XL - Multi-OS packaging experiment with Node, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Python compatibility unknowns; split the proof into platform work.
Complexity is a provisional scope/uncertainty estimate, not a delivery-time commitment. XL work must be split into executable subtasks before starting.
**Planning priority:** P0 - Architecture/foundation work that unblocks the implementation path.
<!-- dozu-tracking:end -->

## Outcome
Recommend Electron with the existing Next.js standalone server, Express and local data/services. Validate packaged behavior instead of creating a second React/Vite UI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Run a native packaged proof on Windows/macOS/Linux with full Next server semantics, local Express, PostgreSQL/pgvector and FastAPI/model.
- [ ] Verify Electron utilityProcess compatibility or bundle a pinned standalone Node runtime; no system Node/Python/database/Docker/WSL requirement.
- [ ] Exercise dynamic routes, locales/server messages, local data writes, files, sockets/streams, PDF/editor/media and a system-browser provider flow.
- [ ] Measure bundle size, RAM/startup, supported CPU/OS and native ABI/dynamic library compatibility; record evidence and resource budgets.
- [ ] Record architecture ADR; the proof is an early gate, not permission to reduce the first-release feature scope.

## Architecture constraints
The complete existing Next.js UI and Express backend run locally with a local database/files. Desktop and local browser use the same localhost backend. Real third-party integrations may use the internet; preserve them wherever feasible. No central Dozu backend, cloud database, synchronization, shared publisher secrets in installers, or simulated replacements. All pages/features remain in release scope.

<!-- dozu-roadmap:DECISION-STACK -->

Phase: 0 Requirements | Priority: P0

Parent roadmap: https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues/1

## Dependencies
- #3 - [Task] Audit complete UI/backend and local-first integration baselines
- #2 - [Ticket] Record local-first requirements and full feature-preservation matrix

comments.body:
Baseline audit #3 is complete. The source-supported Electron/Next standalone + Express + PostgreSQL/pgvector + CPU FastAPI recommendation remains conditional on this proof.

Please include actual additional processing dependencies: Gotenberg/LibreOffice DOC/DOCX/TXT→PDF, Puppeteer URL→PDF/browser assets, whisper.cpp tiny speech model and FFmpeg. No user Docker/WSL/runtime setup can be inherited. Source evidence is in local `planning/audit/systems.md`, `findings.md` and the full page matrix.

Known proof constraints: retained website build currently fails YoutubePlayerAdapter Promise<number>/number type validation; all 20 local migrations are Git-ignored; pgvector extension/first-boot seeds are not established; eager PayOS/mail/Redis initialization prevents a clean optional-provider startup profile. Real CPU 384-dimensional embedding works with the cached model, but batch `/segments/embedding` has an existing response-schema HTTP 500.

This handoff does not start or complete #4, reduce full feature scope, decide #41/#43 or establish all-platform packaging. See #3 completion evidence for commands, source commits and limitations.

User-approved Task #2 contract is now recorded in #2: Windows 10 22H2 legacy/Windows 11 primary x86-64, macOS 13+ Intel/ARM64, Ubuntu 22.04/Debian 12 x86-64; NSIS exe/dmg/deb (MSI optional, AppImage where compatible). Minimum 4 GB RAM/2 GB free/dual-core; low-resource mode required. Targets: 250 MB installer, 750 MB installed; minimum cold UI 10s/warm 5s/backend 8s/normal app memory 700 MB; recommended 5s/3s/4s/1 GB. Account for all runtimes/models/assets/processes. Benchmark in production on agreed minimum configurations; report evidence and an explicit recommendation before changing targets. SQLite is evaluation-only pending backend/vector/SQL/migration compatibility proof. LAN classrooms selected; payment execution explicitly deferred under #41. Read #2 for the full hardware/display/data lifecycle contract. This is a requirements handoff, not benchmark/packaging evidence.
